title: Pangolins Are Some of the Most Illegally Trafficked Animals on the Planet. A Rediscovered Species Could Help - Nautilus
gist: After more than five years of study, researchers reinstated the pangolin species Manis aurita, first named almost 190 years ago. It lives in the forests of Nepal and Northern India and is distinct from the pangolins in China. Pangolins are critically endangered and heavily trafficked for scales used in traditional medicine and for meat.

insights.claim: Pangolins in Africa and Asia are critically endangered and among the most trafficked animals. They are poached for scales used in traditional medicine and for meat that is considered a luxury.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Demand for wildlife trade drives enforcement, supply-chain compliance and zoonotic-risk policy.
